title: Deflate a retained catheter balloon before withdrawing the catheter
instruction: On the inert catheter-care phantom, support the movable blue balloon valve with one hand and connect the free empty needle-free receiver syringe with the other. Allow its plunger to return until the retention balloon collapses. Pull the receiver axially at least 12 mm to disconnect it, then withdraw the catheter completely through the neck. Rest the catheter shaft across the receiving tray and return the syringe to its pad, release both objects and keep both gripper centres at least 60 mm clear for one second. Keep the balloon collapsed throughout withdrawal; do not disconnect before deflation or pull an inflated balloon through the neck.
context: Registered nurses handle catheter removal as part of routine device care. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics counted 3,465,400 registered nursing jobs in 2025. This bench task isolates a mechanical difficulty in that work. The valve rotates freely on a short branch, so the two hands have to support and align separate parts. Returning the receiver plunger changes whether the retained end can physically clear the neck. One hand must keep the valve supported while the other connects and empties the receiver. The fixture is an inert training device. See the registered-nurse occupation profile and the public catheter-care source in the README.
setup:
Coordinates are metres in the calibrated bimanual YAM station. X points forward, Y left and Z up. The table is at z = 0.7475 and the draped support at z = 0.7615. Seed 0 starts both stock parallel grippers open in READY. The setup image is taken after 30 settling controls.

Chamber and retained shaft. A clear polymer cutaway chamber, with radii 75 × 65 × 45 mm, sits at (0.375, 0.125, 0.851) on a 183 × 185 × 9 mm base. Its 46 mm silicone neck has a 12 mm bore along Y. Its centre is (0.375, 0.039, 0.851), with inner and outer planes at y = 0.062 and 0.016. The 40 g rigid shaft has a silicone appearance and is 244 mm long and 6 mm in diameter. Its initial root is (0.375, −0.045, 0.851). Relative to this root, the balloon centre is at y = 132 mm and the distal tip at y = 168 mm. The inflated envelope has a 15 mm radius; the collapsed envelope has a 4 mm radius. The 30 mm long, 18 mm diameter polymer hub carries a 28 × 27 × 12 mm blue tab.

Valve and receiver. The 25 g valve begins at (0.339038, −0.115365, 0.851), yawed −35°. It has a 30 × 24 × 20 mm grip, a 16 mm deep socket and a freely rotating branch to the hub. The 100 g polymer receiver begins at (0.300, 0.300, 0.820) in two open polymer cradles on a 160 × 125 × 10 mm steel pad. Its barrel is 90 × 24 mm, its nozzle 16 × 8 mm, and its flange 43 × 18 mm. The 15 g plunger has a 32 × 25 mm thumb pad and 55 mm available travel. It starts fully forward.

Supports and collection. A polypropylene ledge under the valve tab and two narrow ledges under the hub hold the device at reset. All three are open on top, so the arms can lift the device. A stainless 180 × 380 mm receiving tray sits at (0.240, −0.341), with its floor at z = 0.829 and rim at z = 0.847. Two HDPE V rests inside the tray sit at x = 0.250 and y = −0.220 and −0.370. They support the shaft across the tray while the free valve settles. The storage datum is 30 mm forward of the geometric tray centre. The bundled layout files give each support's dimensions, orientation and mounting position.
scoring:
Grade the last valid 20 Hz observation. Read device pose and plunger travel relative to the valve, fingertip contacts against each device, neck crossings, and the final positions and speeds. At reset or if no milestone qualifies, score 0. Either hand may support the valve.

0.10 — Connect the empty receiver. Nozzle insertion must be 1–7 mm, lateral error at most 2 mm and axis error at most 10°. Alignment must persist for at least 0.15 s with both bodies below 0.10 m/s. The connection starts within 5 mm of zero plunger stroke. At connection and until first full deflation, both pads of one gripper must each register at least 0.05 N against the valve and both opposite pads at least 0.05 N against the barrel. Rest contact does not count.

0.40 — With the valve connected, measured receiver travel reaches at least 49.75 mm from its connection stroke, drained fraction at least 99.5% and balloon collision radius at most 5 mm. Reverse travel while the fluid path remains open recomputes the drained fraction. The 0.40 tier is lost if the balloon reinflates.

0.70 — After full deflation, the receiver pulls axially at least 12 mm from its connected position and the detent releases. Disconnection must be observed on an earlier control than the balloon's first entry into the neck at y = 0.062. Keep the balloon collapsed, pass through the neck within 3 mm of its centreline at both planes, and move the distal tip past y = 0.006.

1.00 — Maintain release for 20 consecutive controls (one second). The disconnected shaft midpoint lies within 25 mm in X and 35 mm in Y of (0.240, −0.311), at z = 0.868–0.888, within 10° of horizontal. The barrel lies within 25 mm horizontally of (0.300, 0.300), at z = 0.805–0.835. Both TCPs stay at least 60 mm from the sampled device points. Every tracked body moves at most 15 mm/s and 0.2 rad/s. Video also shows the fingers clear of the devices.

A missing opposing grasp during connection or first deflation, early disconnection, attached withdrawal, an inflated balloon entering the throat, a neck crossing outside the corridor, reinflation after extraction, or a body root below z = 0.710 permanently zeros the trial. Invalid start or missing/nonfinite measurements cannot establish success. For hardware scoring on the inert phantom, use four independently tared normal-force pads (one on each fingertip), with sensing faces flush to the normal jaw surfaces, a 0.01 N or finer readout, and synchronized 20 Hz force and video. Before each trial check each channel with a calibrated gauge at 0.05 N and 0.20 N and re-tare it unloaded. At the first aligned connection and each control through the first full deflation, use the side and top views to identify each finger's device. Both pads on one hand must read at least 0.05 N against the valve and both on the other hand at least 0.05 N against the barrel; table or rest contact does not qualify. Use the same sampled comparisons as the simulation. This is a specified hardware judging procedure, not a reported hardware measurement.
run_limit: 3,600 control steps at 20 Hz (180 simulated seconds), one episode, seed 0.
fidelity: An inert cutaway uses a rigid 244 mm catheter, a freely jointed valve branch, and a two-size balloon envelope driven by measured plunger return. A finite axial connector models the needle-free valve. Native fingertip-to-device forces verify the supporting and syringe hands. Neck clearance, parking and release use measured poses. The model omits tissue, clinical force calibration and continuous fluid flow. No patient or hardware trial was performed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 3091 steps.
reset_notes: Start a fresh scene and scorer. Put the rigid shaft at (0.375, −0.045, 0.851) and the valve at (0.339038, −0.115365, 0.851), yaw −35°. Keep the hub and valve tabs on the open staging ledges. Put the receiver and plunger at (0.300, 0.300, 0.820) with identity rotation and stroke within 5 mm of zero. The recovery tray is empty. Restore the inflated collision envelope, clear the receiver connection and all score history, and leave both arms open in READY. Settle for 30 controls at 20 Hz before taking the setup photo or starting the score. The layout uses a new, independent initialization between trials.
